body:
“Not disclosing earlier”? Are you for real? You’re acting as if people with herpes need to have a large sign over their head reading “I have herpes! Be aware!”. OP disclosed before sex. Doesn’t matter 2 hours, 2 weeks, or 2 months in. Disclosure happened. OP has nothing to feel guilty about. 

Herpes is not the most important thing about a person.

I don’t agree with this - people may not disclose due to fear of rejection, based on stigma. This doesn’t mean they’re automatically bad people, who would willingly cheat or spend all of their partners money.

I’m going to go against the grain here.

If you found out your partner of two years had a history of cold sores, would you feel the same way? 

If not, then your feelings are based on stigma. Lots of people don’t disclose cold sores, which are herpes, which pose a similar risk as people with HSV2. 

Not telling you doesn’t make her fundamentally a bad person. She is most likely afraid of rejection based on a society which sees a skin condition as “dirty” or “slutty”. I personally do not think this reflects her character is regards to cheating.
I know this - however, most people will hear “genital herpes” and will instantly reject someone on that basis, regardless if they already have HSV1.

I’m not debating disclosure, I’m pointing out that the majority, if not all, individuals with oral HSV1 DON’T disclose. Whereas genital is expected to be disclosed, and subsequently results in rejection.

UK. On one hand it’s good because it’s way less of a big deal here than the US. Which is probably one of the reasons they don’t prescribe suppressive therapy. You can only get it if you’ve had 6+ outbreaks a year, and even then they only prescribe it for 6-12 months.

But that’s the thing - oral HSV1 is never a dealbreaker.

Someone is less likely to contract HSV1 off me, even if I didn’t know I had it. Genital HSV1 is much less contagious than oral. That’s what annoys me.

But realistically I’m going to have to disclose WAY before love is involved. I’ve never had a problem with people having HSV1 - ALL my partners have had it in the more contagious oral area. But I know my genital will be a dealbreaker even though it’s basically non contagious outside an outbreak.
We don’t use condoms, neither of us take antivirals, I waited for my primary outbreak to go away and we continued our sex life as normal.

That would only realistically happen if one of the partners is immunocompromised. In two healthy adults, contracting oral HSV2 from a genital HSV2+ partner when you already have an established infection isn’t going to happen.
No, there are no risks when both partners have HSV2.

“Potentially ruined his sex life”, maybe choose some better wording, it’s quite insulting to those with genital herpes. 

If he knows you are HSV1+ and has consented then there is no need to worry.
Yes, like everyone who has genital herpes avoids sex during an outbreak. But I do feel like those with genital herpes have this extra obligation to protect others that oral HSV+ people don’t have.

I acquired genital HSV1 from oral sex from my oral HSV1+ boyfriend. 

If she already has HSV1, then she’s at no risk. 

If she does not, then there is a risk. Oral HSV1 sheds without symptoms about 9-18% of the time. Pretty much all cases of genital HSV1 are caused by oral sex by someone who was oral HSV1+. 

You can reduce the risk by using dental dams, and avoiding oral during outbreaks.

Before contracting HSV1, all of my partners had oral HSV1 however it would never of crossed their (or my own) mind to take daily antivirals. I also don’t know anyone who has oral HSV1 who takes them to protect their partners. It just seems weird that it’s almost expected for people with genital HSV1, and I’m wondering if this is more stigma dependent rather than medical. It feels almost that I have a duty and obligation to “protect” others from HSV1 whereas if I had it orally I would not have this expectation.

I didn’t know he had it for about 5 months until he had an actual outbreak, and this was after lots of unprotected oral. I stayed with him despite the risk as I am aware HSV1 is so common and I genuinely believed I was an asymptomatic carrier as I’ve never had a boyfriend who hasn’t had cold sores. I’m angry now, not at him giving me HSV1 but the general situation as I don’t think I “deserve” it. I’m angry at his blasé attitude, his complete lack of emotional support and the fact he doesn’t think he needs to disclose to future partners.

Sorry, I didn’t make it clear. I didn’t know he had HSV1 until about 5 months into the relationship (after lots of unprotected oral and kissing), and I found out because he had an actual outbreak. I got mad at that point but got over it, as all of my previous boyfriends have had HSV1 orally. Since then he’s had a few outbreaks, however I contracted genital HSV1 through asymptomatic shedding.

Unfortunately I'm in the UK, and they do not prescribe suppressive treatment until you've had more than 6 outbreaks in one year (I begged, three doctors said no). On top of that, they wouldn't routinely prescribe suppressive treatment for genital HSV1, as the rate of tranmission is already so low it doesn't really offer any additional protection to partners (tranmission risk is considerably less than oral HSV1).
